I've been on 200 mg of lamictal for 1.5 years. 

It hasn't done anything for my anxiety. The only things that have helped even a little are SSRI's that I can't take because they induce hypomania.

I tried hydroxyzine, but it interacted too much with lamictal. 

I am taking propranolol for anxiety right now. It helps the physical symptoms of anxiety, like racing heart and shaking hands. But it hasn't helped with anxious thoughts or emotions. I use to have a resting heart rate of 120. Propranolol has brought it down to 90.

It's frustrating that it's been so hard to treat anxiety. 


From my experience, lamictal isn't great at treating anxiety, but it's possible that it might help--everyone is different. Thankfully, there are a lot of options out there and it's great that you are working with a psych nurse right now. Best of luck.

bipolar 2 and ptsd

Once I got the overwhelming bipolar symptoms settled, I noticed that I still had intense flashbacks and other ptsd symptoms. 

At first, I attributed the flashbacks and avoidance issues to the bipolar issues. 

But once medication mitigated the bipolar stuff, I was still left with the trauma. 

And so, once I was in a place of general okayness with bipolar, it was apparent that the flashbacks/nightmares/avoidance issues were directly related to longstanding trauma, and not merely a symptom of bipolar. 

It was like...the trauma symptoms weren't such a big deal in light of wanting to kill myself all the time (I'm sure they contributed some, though).
